recipe: recipe.toml (the shipped `governance` ontology-v1 template, with corpus.id/name and acquire.path filled)
note: Ground truth for the ontology-v1 P4 equivalence case (ONTOLOGY_MIGRATION.md §P4, order ontology-v1-p4 'Done when'). The point is NOT tension recall — maple-house already covers that. The point is the one case the deontic reading and the `equivalent` verdict exist for: two surface forms of ONE rule must yield one rule, not two, and NOT a conflict. Invented house, invented decisions.

rules.section: Article VII — Hosting in the common room
rules.subject: T-hosting
rules.text: Hosting must end by 10pm on weeknights.

rules.subject: T-hosting
rules.text: Members must not host in the common room after 10pm on weeknights.

rules.subject: T-quiet
rules.text: Weekend quiet hours in the common room begin at 11pm.

rules.subject: T-parking
rules.text: Guests may park in the visitor bay for up to four hours.

rules.subject: T-parking
rules.text: The visitor bay is not for overnight guest parking.

expected_equivalences.why: The SAME rule in two surface forms: `require (hosting ends by 10pm)` and `forbid (hosting after 10pm)` are interdefined. The Phase-6 classifier must return `relation: "equivalent"` with `is_tension: false`, which materialises ONE `same_as` Claim (grade `classifier`) and NO Tension edge. This is the case `render_phase6_extras`'s `## Deontic reading` section exists for.

expected_supersessions.why: Once E1 links them (a `same_as` claim), `change.supersedes = { rule = "valid" }` folds the older onto the newer clock: R1 becomes `RuleStatus::SupersededByClock { by_rules: [R2] }` and R2 stays Active. Without the link the pair must NOT fold — that is what `derive_active_with_policy_folds_linked_only` pins.

expected_non_tensions.why: Different topics (hosting vs quiet hours) and different days (weeknight vs weekend). `tension.same = ["subject", "valid"]` should drop this pair before the classifier ever sees it — different subject.

Same topic, overlapping validity, so the pair IS comparable and does reach the classifier. `permit (4h in the bay)` and `forbid (overnight in the bay)` are compatible — one bounds the other. The author's own `not_conflicts` names 'two separate exemptions to the same rule'.
Different subjects again — the Maple House decoy class, two rules sharing the word 'guest' and governing nothing in common.

bars.one_rule_not_two: After `enrich build --full`, the governance view lists exactly ONE active rule on topic `hosting`.
bars.no_conflict: `atlas/edges.json` carries no Tension edge between the Article VII rule and the 2025-03-14 decision.
bars.reified: `atlas/atoms.json` carries one Claim with `claim_kind == "same_as"` and `attributes.grade == "classifier"` naming both.
